subject: Renewal: Capacity top-up & throughput commitment (addendum request)
messages:
From: Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@falkon.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Falkon AI Procurement <procurement@falkon.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + capacity expansion: request for throughput commitment

Hi Marissa,

Our renewal with Redwood is up for signature on April 15. Over the last quarter our workload has grown faster than expected and we need to expand our dedicated pool ahead of the renewal. Specifically: we want to add eight (8) A100 GPUs to our reserved pool and formalize a throughput commitment in the contract addendum so engineering can rely on steady inference capacity during peak launches.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide an addendum that commits to 250,000 tokens/sec (p95) for the combined reserved pool, measured monthly (or rolling 30-day window) with defined measurement methodology and an SLA credit table for missed SLOs? We also need a capacity schedule (dates for provisioning) and a note on billing/proration for the April 15 effective date.

I'll loop in procurement for PO coordination. Attached is a one-page traffic forecast to justify the request.

Thanks,
Greg Tanner
Head of Platform
Falkon AI
Attachments: falkon_forecast_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity expansion: request for throughput commitment

Greg —

Thanks for the context and the forecast. Happy to push this through for an April 15 amendment. I'm looping in Sergio (solutions) to size the throughput profile and Dev (legal/renewals) to draft the addendum language and credit table.

Next steps from our side:
- Sergio: produce an SLO draft and a capacity schedule showing when we can provision +8 A100s.
- Dev: draft addendum with measurement methodology and credit mechanics.
- I: consolidate and send a single addendum + capacity schedule for your review and procurement.

Question for you: do you prefer measurement as a calendar-month metric or a rolling 30-day window? Procurement sometimes asks for calendar months for invoicing simplicity.

I'll aim to send the first draft by Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Lead Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: SLO draft and provisioning cadence for Falkon capacity top-up

Marissa / Dev / Laura —

Attached is a technical SLO draft and a capacity schedule workbook (capacity_schedule_Q2.xlsx) that maps the +8 A100s provisioning in two waves: 4 GPUs on Apr 15 (effective date) and the remaining 4 on May 1. The draft SLO uses tokens/sec measured at ingress, aggregated across the reserved pool. Key points:

- Proposed SLO: 250,000 tokens/sec (p95) measured per calendar month across the reserved pool.
- Measurement: 5-minute sampling intervals; monthly aggregation; exclude scheduled maintenance windows with >30m advance notice.
- Fallback: automatic routing to compatible burst capacity if sustained utilization hits 95% of committed throughput for >10 minutes.
- Credit tiers: 5% credit for p95 < 250k but >= 230k; 10% credit for p95 < 230k but >= 200k; 25% for p95 < 200k.

I've attached slo_table.csv with example calculations and a suggested phrasing for the addendum. This is intentionally conservative on credits to balance Falkon's need for predictability and our desire to limit open-ended liability.

If you want the measurement window to be rolling-30 we can change the wording; note that rolling windows require a slightly different billing/reporting cadence (we can still deliver).

-- Sergio
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo_addendum_draft_v3.pdf, capacity_schedule_Q2.xlsx, slo_table.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLO draft and provisioning cadence for Falkon capacity top-up

Marissa / Sergio —

Quick legal redlines on the addendum (see addendum_redline_v2.pdf):
- Measurement: prefer "calendar month" as Marissa suggested — clearer for invoicing and crediting. If Falkon insists on rolling 30-day, we need explicit reconciliation steps.
- Definitions: define "tokens/sec" as "effective input tokens per second measured at the service ingress point, averaged over 5-minute intervals."
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and customer-caused throttling must be explicit.
- Remedies: cap aggregate credits in any 12-month period to 3 months' fees for the reserved pool. (Negotiable but we should propose a cap.)
- Termination right: if we miss the SLOs for 3 consecutive months and remedies are exhausted, add limited termination right for Falkon. Legal prefers an alternative remedy route rather than immediate termination.

I'll incorporate these into the draft addendum and highlight the redlines for negotiation. Also added a short clause around measurement tooling and dashboard links so Falkon can validate metrics.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: addendum_redline_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@falkon.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Falkon AI Procurement <procurement@falkon.ai>
Date: 2026-03-30T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft addendum & capacity schedule for review (effective Apr 15)

Greg —

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. Attached is the consolidated addendum (slo_addendum_draft_v3.pdf) and the capacity schedule (capacity_schedule_Q2.xlsx) aligned to an Apr 15 effective date with proration for April. Highlights:

- Capacity: +8 A100 GPUs to reserved pool in two waves (4 on Apr 15, 4 on May 1).
- SLO: 250,000 tokens/sec (p95), measured per calendar month, with 5-minute sampling intervals.
- Credits: tiered credit table as suggested by Sergio; legal has added exclusions and a maximum aggregate credit cap.
- Measurement access: we will provide a read-only dashboard link for metric validation and weekly reports during the first 90 days.
- Billing: first invoice will be prorated for Apr 15–Apr 30 and then monthly thereafter; procurement should include PO referencing DL-2026-FALK-0091.

Next steps: please review the addendum and tell us any redlines by COB Apr 2. If this looks fine, supply a PO and we'll push the DocuSign package. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the SLO wording if helpful.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Lead Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: slo_addendum_draft_v3.pdf, capacity_schedule_Q2.xlsx

Appreciate the quick turnaround — reviewed with platform and procurement. A couple of small asks:
1) Can we change measurement from "calendar month" to "calendar month with a monthly reconciliation report"? We want month-bound guarantees but also a standard reconciliation export for our finance team.
2) Can the credit cap be expressed in dollars as an alternate (e.g., cap at $X) instead of "3 months' fees"? Procurement needs a dollar figure for PO planning.

We'll aim to get any redlines back today. Also, please share the DocuSign link when ready.

— Greg
